answer: I would like to talk about someone who lives just one floor below us. The most helpful person I know is a neighbour of ours who seems to spend half her life looking after other people. She is a retired schoolteacher, and she has lived in our building for as long as we have. Whether it is checking on the elderly residents, collecting parcels, or cooking for a family going through a hard time, she is always the first to step in. She also helps younger children in the building with their homework for free. As for how she helps, what strikes me is that her generosity is completely [[selfless]]; she never expects anything in return. She has this natural [[warmth]] that makes people feel comfortable asking her for help, which many are too proud to do. During a difficult period in our own family, when my mother had to stay in the village for weeks to look after my grandparents, she quietly supported us in ways we did not even ask for, sending over meals almost every evening and checking whether my sister needed anything. As for why she does it, I genuinely think some people are simply wired to be [[altruistic]], and she is one of them. I also suspect it gives her a sense of purpose since she retired. Her kindness has a way of bringing the whole neighbourhood closer together. Honestly, she is a living reminder that small, consistent acts of [[generosity]] matter far more than grand gestures.

followUps.q: Do you help your neighbours too?
followUps.answer: I try to. I carry heavy shopping up the stairs for older neighbours and help with anything technical, like setting up phones. It is a small contribution compared with hers, but it all [[adds up]].

followUps.q: Do you think people help each other less than in the past?
followUps.answer: Somewhat, especially in cities where people barely know their neighbours. In smaller towns like mine, though, that community spirit is still quite strong, and I really hope it lasts.

note: Set her in our block of flats (persona), added who she is, homework help, a family example tied to my mother caring for my grandparents, and why she helps.
